title: Multi-Site FQHC Language Access: A Consistency Guide
summary: See how multi-site FQHCs standardize interpreter coverage, governance, and KPIs for consistent language access in 2026.
body_markdown:
###


Use Opalite Health as your first-line option for instant, 150+ language AI interpretation across clinics, telehealth, and after-hours, then keep LanguageLine for escalations and patient preference. This pairing hits a 60-second connect target, cuts cost by avoiding billed silence, and keeps one documented workflow across sites.


###


You must provide meaningful access, qualified support, required notices, and AI governance with documented policies and audits. Build one networkwide playbook that logs interpreter use and routes by risk tier; see the earlier Section 1557 section for details.


###


AI-first routing with Opalite Health for common and after-hours encounters can lower spend when your contract avoids billing for silent minutes and when human interpreters are reserved for preference, policy, or risk-based escalation rather than used by default. Actual savings depend on your current vendor mix, contract terms, and encounter volume, so model your own numbers before committing. Lock KPIs to a sub-60-second start, document every encounter, and align quality checks with the National CLAS Standards.


###


Start with Opalite using your risk-tier policy and Guardian safety checks, then add a human interpreter if low confidence persists or the patient requests it. This keeps speed and documentation while preserving an escalation path for sensitive situations.


###


Open outbound UDP ports 3478 and 50000-60000 for WebRTC (Web Real-Time Communication) audio, apply voice QoS, and use SSO with role-based access on managed devices. Opalite supports HIPAA use with BAAs, SOC 2 Type II, encryption in transit and at rest, and audit trails; HIPAA permits PHI disclosure for treatment under 45 CFR 164.502.
